origins: When favorite pastimes like reading, music, conversation, or driving become hard or impossible, we mourn them. Without new sources of joy, life can seem gray.
teaches: “You have made known to me the path of life; You will fill me with joy in Your presence.” “The LORD is my strength and my song.” “Sorrowful, yet always rejoicing.” Joy is not tied to one sense. Other senses sharpen, new hobbies appear, and nearness to God and people remain. Grieve what you cannot do, and then look for what you can: audio books, music, touch, taste, conversation, prayer, nature’s sounds or scents.
self_statements: There is nothing to look forward to.
errors: Believing life is either full or joyless.
Predicting that joy is gone for good.
Feeling grief and concluding that life is no longer enjoyable.
questions: What did I love that I can no longer do as before?
What adaptations might return some of it?
What new sources of joy could I try?
What moments of joy have I had recently?
What does Scripture say about joy in God’s presence?
Whom can I enjoy things with?
truth: Joy is not gone. It may look different. I can grieve what I have lost, try adaptations and new pleasures, and find joy in God’s presence and in people.
hw_truths: The Lord fills me with joy in His presence.
He is my strength and my song.
I can be sorrowful yet rejoicing.
log: Each week, note one thing you enjoyed, old or new.
actions: Find a way to do an old pleasure differently.
Audio books, music, crafts, or a walk with a friend.
prayer: Lord, joy has faded. Fill me with joy in Your presence, and show me new things to love. Amen.
